page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-60 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Tau T2D instance family. Powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, it is configured with 60 dedicated vCPUs mapped 1:1 to 60 physical cores with a single thread per core. Memory capacity totals 240 GB, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4 GB per core). The processor features 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core complex, with support for cryptographic acceleration sets including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, as well as AVX and BMI2 instruction extensions. The instance includes no bundled local NVMe storage and does not feature GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded computational efficiency. In the stress-ng multi-core CPU benchmark, the t2d-standard-60 achieves top-tier results in the upper 10%, while PassMark CPU and Geekbench multi-core scores land squarely in the top 25%. High-parallelism tasks like Clang compilation, ray tracing, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression show strong throughput due to the non-hyperthreaded physical core architecture. In memory tests, cached reads reach strong levels, whereas uncached large-block reads and writes fall into the middle 50%. In-memory database workloads demonstrate solid capability, delivering 86.31 million Redis SET operations per second.

Hardware tradeoffs center around instruction set compatibility and local storage options. While the AMD EPYC architecture provides strong integer throughput and dedicated core execution without hyperthreading contention, it lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions. This is reflected in Large Language Model (LLM) inference benchmarks, where large 70B parameter text generation ranks in the bottom 10%. Furthermore, because the instance carries no local storage out of the box, all disk I/O must rely on attached network persistent disks.

The t2d-standard-60 provides balanced cost efficiency for enterprise-scale workloads requiring sustained thread isolation and robust multi-core scaling. Ideal use cases include multi-threaded software build pipelines, high-density web application serving, batch ETL processing, containerized microservice orchestrators, and memory-resident databases such as Redis.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-60 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, delivering 60 dedicated vCPUs on 60 physical cores (1 thread per core) paired with 240 GB of RAM. The instance lacks bundled local storage and GPU hardware, depending on network storage for persistence. In benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded compute performance in stress-ng and strong scores in Geekbench multi-core, Clang compilation, and Redis operations (86.31 million SET ops/sec). The absence of AVX-512 extensions limits large LLM text generation throughput, making heavy AI inference less optimal. With its 1:4 core-to-memory ratio and dedicated physical execution threads, the instance delivers dependable, cost-efficient scaling for compute-heavy batch processing, parallel CI/CD compilation, enterprise web applications, and in-memory key-value databases.
